decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom took heavy development investment and was announced publicly as a release for a strategic segment, so even though its website presence weakened in 2019, management would attribute this to the slow pace of particle therapy installations and persist with it.

Small volume ionization chambers belong to the firm's core dosimetry identity and were consistently given their own page, so dropping one would undercut the established portfolio and its accredited calibration base.

Despite overlapping with the other small volume chamber, it sits within the firm's committed core detector line with ongoing calibration and support obligations, which makes withdrawal unlikely in the near term.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a staple product tied to the firm's decades of dosimetry experience and its installed clinical base, so there is strong reason to keep it.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantoms and QA workflows that are central to its announced platform direction, and nothing suggests its weakness is permanent.
Thimble chambers are core, low-cost line items the firm has visibly committed to, so it has little incentive to write them off.
